Even Apple CEO Tim Cook has admitted that the Vision Pro is a niche product. This author has also previously pointed out that this device is a necessary step toward the more consumer-friendly and affordable Apple Glasses.

However, it is worth noting that sometimes niche products can play a significant role in professional fields, and a new surgical study clearly demonstrates why this matters to both patients and surgeons...

The use of Vision Pro in surgery is on the rise

Endoscopic surgery involves using miniature instruments passed through thin tubes, with surgeons operating while watching the camera feed on a display in the operating room. Performing surgery this way results in much smaller incisions and significantly shorter recovery times for patients.

Many surgeons have already switched from traditional displays to the Vision Pro headset. As far back as two and a half years ago, a renowned neurosurgeon had already applied it in multiple spinal reconstruction surgeries. Other doctors have also stated that the device can reduce pain and discomfort for surgeons, and even lower the risk of injury.

This headset has also been adopted by other members of the surgical team, including a senior scrub nurse, who described the device as making it virtually impossible to make mistakes when anticipating which tools the surgeon will need next.

This device has also been used to help surgeons plan and visualise procedures before passing them to surgical robots for execution, as well as to aid visualisation during conventional surgery.

At $3,500, the price may not be considered cheap for the average consumer, but compared to traditional operating room displays—which cost $20,000 each—it is actually very affordable.

"Faster and better"

Analyst Horace Dediu participated in a peer-reviewed study at the University of California, San Diego, demonstrating the value of Vision Pro for surgeons. The study found that replacing traditional displays with the Vision Pro headset brought multiple benefits for both doctors and patients.

The study compared surgeries performed using traditional displays with those using Vision Pro, and found the latter had several advantages.

• Surgery time reduced by 19% • Functional success rate of 100%, with no complications during or after surgery • Surgeons reported significantly reduced workload, with all participating doctors expressing a preference for the Apple Vision Pro experience • Improved ergonomics, allowing surgeons to maintain a natural, forward-facing posture

So while the Vision Pro is indeed a developing tool paving the way for a truly consumer-facing product, in the right hands it already holds significant value in its own right.
